clue.text: Threat suggested by one forever taking tea

definitions.meaning: surface reading: something menacing is hinted at by a guest at a tea party
setter's reading: the answer itself, read as an instruction, rearranges a six-letter word into the word Threat

explanation.surface: A tea-drinker who never leaves the table hints at some menace.
explanation.walkthrough: A reverse clue: in MAD HATTER, MAD tells you to rearrange HATTER, which gives THREAT. So the answer suggests the word Threat.
explanation.definitionFit: In Alice in Wonderland this character is stuck at a never-ending tea party because Time stopped at six o'clock.

clue.text: Chitty-Chitty Bang-Bang, say, favourite fairytale transport

parts.note: the flying car in the film is an example of an enchanted motor
a teacher's pet is the favourite

explanation.surface: The famous flying car is offered as the best-loved vehicle of storybooks.
explanation.definitionFit: Flying rugs carry heroes through the Arabian Nights and other folk tales, a classic storybook way to travel.

clue.text: In getting up fast, I remedy fault

indicators.note: in a down clue, rising means the letters read from bottom to top
the letters wanted sit inside the run of words that follows

parts.note: letters running across the end of fast, the I and most of remedy

explanation.surface: Someone recovering from a fast says they will put a problem right.
explanation.definitionFit: A demerit is a mark against someone, a bad point or failing.

clue.text: Sort of lamp I plugged in picked up as benefit

indicators.note: in a down clue, lifting the word up makes it read upwards, back to front
something plugged in is pushed inside another thing

parts.note: a lava lamp has blobs of wax rising and falling

explanation.surface: A lamp with a plug is collected because it will be useful.
explanation.definitionFit: Avail as a noun means use or advantage, as in 'to no avail'.

clue.text: Prepare vegetables and quickly see to baby

definitions.meaning: first meaning: cut off both ends of beans or carrots
second meaning: wash an infant's face and bottom only

explanation.surface: A busy parent cooks supper and attends to the infant at once.
explanation.definitionFit: Trimming the ends of produce and a brief wash of face and bottom are both called by this phrase.

clue.text: Met together for cause: Republican joined

explanation.surface: A Republican signs up with a group meeting for a political cause.
explanation.definitionFit: Supporters who rallied came together in a body to support a shared aim.

clue.text: Fun in summer from people in lawsuits being on weed?

parts.note: to weed is to work in the garden, used here as a verb
the sides in a legal case are the parties

explanation.surface: Litigants high on cannabis are having a jolly summer time.
explanation.walkthrough: In an across clue, 'being on' puts the litigants after the weeding word.
explanation.definitionFit: Outdoor social gatherings with tea and cake on the lawn are a staple of English summers.

clue.text: Smooth style of progress through various gears? Nonsense

indicators.note: the first pieces pass through the middle of the mixed word
various suggests the letters come in a different, mixed order

parts.note: taken as written, to be mixed
to sand is to smooth with sandpaper
a gait is a manner of walking

explanation.surface: A driver's smooth gear-changing is dismissed as rubbish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Smooth' and 'style of progress' look like a description of driving, but each gives its own word. Gas and gaiters comes from Dickens.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means pompous, empty talk, from the speech of a mad old gentleman in Nicholas Nickleby.

clue.text: Before test, drops coat

parts.note: a proof is a trial or test

explanation.surface: Someone takes off a coat just before an examination.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Before' places the drops ahead of the test; 'drops coat' looks like removing clothing.
explanation.definitionFit: As a noun this is a waterproof overcoat, a garment that keeps out the wet.

clue.text: Construction of poem featuring in Eliot's first gamble

indicators.note: first asks for only the opening letter of the name

parts.note: opening letter of the poet's name

indicators.note: something featuring in another appears inside it

explanation.surface: A poem appears in a work by T.S. Eliot about chance.
explanation.walkthrough: The poem is Kipling's famous two-letter title, not one of Eliot's.
explanation.definitionFit: An edifice is a large building, a structure that has been put up.

clue.text: Greek visionary's plans then lie in ruins

indicators.note: plans in ruins have been wrecked, so the letters are broken up and rebuilt

explanation.surface: A Greek dreamer's schemes collapse, like the ruins of ancient Greece.
explanation.definitionFit: A Panhellenist dreams of uniting all Greeks in one political whole, an idealistic vision.

clue.text: Get back from city in sheer delight

indicators.note: in places the first item inside the second

parts.note: EC is the postcode area of the City of London

explanation.surface: Someone recovers something, and a city erupts in delight.
explanation.definitionFit: To recapture is to retake or regain something that was lost.

clue.text: Ditch, I hear, with predictable exceptions gets more slippery

indicators.note: the letters left out follow a regular, predictable pattern, every other one

parts.note: even-placed letters of these three words

explanation.surface: A spelling rule about 'I before E' seems to be cited, with its usual exceptions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'I hear' and 'exceptions' suggest a sound-alike or the i-before-e rule; in fact you keep every second letter of Ditch I hear.
explanation.definitionFit: Icier roads have more ice on them and so are harder to grip.

clue.text: Runner's up prizes on high quality race track

parts.note: tone in the sense of class or refinement, as in 'lowering the tone'

explanation.surface: Second-place awards are handed out at a top-class racing venue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Runner's up' disguises runners-up; in a down clue 'on' stacks the first part above the second.
explanation.definitionFit: Silverstone in Northamptonshire is the motor-racing circuit that hosts the British Grand Prix.

clue.text: Poor mark in school given by master

parts.note: a gam is a school of whales

explanation.surface: A teacher at school gives a pupil a low grade.
explanation.walkthrough: 'School' is not the classroom but a group of whales.
explanation.definitionFit: Gamma, the third Greek letter, is used as a low grade in some marking schemes, below alpha and beta.

clue.text: Arab friend — European gets one for nothing

indicators.note: one letter takes the place of a zero-shaped letter in the word

explanation.surface: A friend from Europe gets something free, Arab-style hospitality perhaps.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gets one for nothing' sounds like a free gift; it means the letter I replaces an O.
explanation.definitionFit: Palestinians are an Arab people of the land between the Jordan and the Mediterranean.

clue.text: Hot and cold, turning unwell, with this?

definitions.text: Hot and cold, turning unwell, with this?

indicators.note: turning round makes the pair of abbreviations swap order

parts.note: H and C, the tap abbreviations

explanation.surface: A patient running hot and cold turns poorly and wonders if this is the cause.
explanation.walkthrough: The tap abbreviations swap round. Read whole, the clue describes the alternating flushes of someone falling ill with this.
explanation.definitionFit: A chill is a feverish cold, with shivering and alternating flushes of heat.

clue.text: Singing happily in America, Scotsman from another era

parts.note: the American spelling, with one L, of singing carols

explanation.surface: A Scotsman joyfully singing in the US seems to belong to the past.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in America' is there for the spelling: British English doubles the L.
explanation.definitionFit: Carolingian describes the Frankish dynasty of Charlemagne, so belongs to a medieval period long past.

clue.text: On power trips, quietly press for expulsion of MPs

parts.note: to press someone is to urge them

explanation.surface: Power-hungry figures push quietly to throw members out of Parliament.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On power' puts the trips after P. Pride's Purge (1648) was Colonel Pride's removal of MPs hostile to the army from the Long Parliament.
explanation.definitionFit: In 1648 Colonel Thomas Pride's soldiers barred some 140 members from the Commons, an event known by this name.

clue.text: Pull vehicle back in a series of races

indicators.note: back says the vehicle word reads from right to left
in puts the turned word inside what follows

parts.note: the Isle of Man TT, Tourist Trophy motorcycle races
a cart is a simple vehicle

explanation.surface: A tow truck reverses to haul a vehicle during a race meeting.
explanation.definitionFit: To attract is to draw or pull something towards oneself.

clue.text: A loveless return for country girl

indicators.note: a return goes back the way it came, so the letters read backwards
without love means the zero-shaped letter is taken away

explanation.surface: A jilted country girl heads back home with no love left.
explanation.walkthrough: Love is O in tennis; drop it from LEBANON and reverse the rest after A.
explanation.definitionFit: Annabel is a female first name.

clue.text: Irritated expression as pet vanished

explanation.surface: An owner swears in annoyance when the family pet disappears.
explanation.definitionFit: Doggone is a mild American exclamation of annoyance, a euphemism for damn.

clue.text: It offers hope to the sick and old, sure to be treated

definitions.text: It offers hope to the sick

indicators.note: treated means processed or worked on, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Something gives hope to elderly patients who are sure to receive treatment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'treated' sits naturally with 'the sick' but is the rearrangement signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Lourdes in France is a Catholic pilgrimage site where many seek miraculous healing at the grotto.

clue.text: Trace family: Nick may do it

parts.note: to draw over lines is to trace

explanation.surface: A genealogist is told to trace their family history.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nick' looks like a name, perhaps a police slang word, but it is a small cut.
explanation.definitionFit: A small cut breaks the skin, and so causes bleeding.

clue.text: What could create current possible disagreement?

explanation.surface: Something topical might spark a falling-out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'current' reads as up to date, but it is electric current.
explanation.definitionFit: Voltage between two points drives electric flow through a conductor, so it creates a current.

clue.text: Traditional accompaniments that are cut off

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the usual side dishes, as with turkey 'and all the ...'
second meaning: offcuts left after clipping

explanation.surface: Customary side dishes are being removed from the table.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both the garnishes served with a roast and the pieces snipped away when tidying.

clue.text: Boat that leads the way for others?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a flat barge used to unload ships

definitions.text: that leads the way for others?
definitions.meaning: second meaning, playful: one who illuminates a path for followers

explanation.surface: A boat heads a convoy, guiding the others behind it.
explanation.definitionFit: A barge for ferrying cargo bears this name, and so jokingly does anyone who shows a route by shining light.

clue.text: Knock over wine for communion

explanation.surface: Knocking over the wine at Holy Communion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Communion' suggests church wine, but it means close understanding; in a down clue 'over' stacks the knock above the wine.
explanation.definitionFit: Rapport is a close, harmonious relationship, a sharing of thoughts and feelings.

clue.text: Back an attempt

explanation.surface: Support someone having a try.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Back' looks like a verb meaning support; it is the adverb, as in years back.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words mean in the past, earlier than now, as in 'ten years ...'.

clue.text: In operetta, what's put before jury? Not a hat

indicators.note: not the letter named next means it is left out

parts.words: In operetta, what's put before jury
parts.note: Trial by Jury is a Gilbert and Sullivan operetta

explanation.surface: A question about what precedes the jury in an operetta title, with a hat thrown in.
explanation.definitionFit: A trilby is a soft felt hat with a narrow brim and indented crown.

clue.text: Terror as dresser goes tipping over, bits smashing off

indicators.note: a piece of furniture tipping over ends up the other way round
pieces knocked off the ends leave only a middle run of letters

parts.note: the end of dresser and the start of goes

explanation.surface: A dresser crashes over and its pieces break off, causing panic.
explanation.definitionFit: An ogress is a female ogre, a fearsome woman, so a terror in the informal sense.

clue.text: The latest worry for museum conservator?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: most modern, cutting-edge
second meaning, playful: the condition of the paintings in their care

explanation.surface: A gallery restorer frets over the newest thing.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means most advanced technology, and literally the condition of artworks a curator must look after.

clue.text: Steps taken as father's old, getting billions in benefit

indicators.note: the benefit word gets something put inside it

explanation.surface: An elderly father on benefits suddenly receives billions.
explanation.definitionFit: The paso doble is a lively Latin ballroom dance modelled on a bullfight, so a set of dance steps.

clue.text: Useless worker endlessly about to finish cell extension

indicators.note: about means going round the next item
without its end means the final letter is cut

parts.note: a drone bee does no work

explanation.surface: An idle worker is about to finish an extension to a prison cell.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cell' suggests prison, but it is a nerve cell; the drone is the male bee that does no work.
explanation.definitionFit: A dendron, or dendrite, is a branching projection of a nerve cell.

clue.text: Antelope eats daisies, including one in remote place

indicators.note: an animal that eats something takes it inside
the flowers take a letter inside them

explanation.surface: A grazing antelope munches flowers somewhere far away.
explanation.walkthrough: Asters belong to the daisy family, so 'daisies' fairly stands for them.
explanation.definitionFit: Easter Island in the South Pacific is one of the most isolated inhabited islands on Earth.

clue.text: Agreeable article for men in tribute

indicators.note: for means one thing stands in place of another

parts.note: a compliment is praise, a tribute

explanation.surface: Men are paid a tribute in a newspaper article.
explanation.definitionFit: Compliant means willing to go along with others, so ready to agree.

clue.text: Winning daily is guaranteed, but not car

indicators.note: but not means the following item is subtracted

parts.note: a daily or char is a cleaning lady

explanation.surface: A daily newspaper boasts that some prize is certain, though not a car.
explanation.walkthrough: A daily is British for a cleaning woman, also called a char.
explanation.definitionFit: Charismatic people have winning charm that draws others to them.

clue.text: Closely follow play, having to put in notice

indicators.note: the play has something inserted into it

parts.note: a show is a theatrical play
an ad is a public notice

explanation.surface: A theatre producer must post a notice for a play.
explanation.definitionFit: To shadow someone is to tail them closely, as a detective does.

clue.text: Walking a very short distance, short of energy

indicators.note: short of means lacking, so a letter is missing

explanation.surface: Someone out of breath manages to walk only a tiny way.
explanation.definitionFit: Travelling on foot means going by walking rather than by vehicle.

clue.text: You're caught; could this describe Quidditch?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: your deception has been found out
second meaning, playful: the sport in Harry Potter is played aloft on broomsticks

explanation.surface: A wizard is caught out mid-match.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom announces that a trick has been discovered; literally, Quidditch is a match played high in the air.

clue.text: Discovered painting in prison: sentence not wasted!

indicators.note: wasted means ruined, so these letters are wrecked and rebuilt

parts.note: doing time is serving a sentence

explanation.surface: A convict finds a painting in jail and makes good use of the sentence.
explanation.definitionFit: A pentimento is an earlier image found beneath the surface of a painting where the artist painted over it.

clue.text: Scotland's own Foreign Department

definitions.meaning: first meaning: Scots dialect for 'own'
second meaning: an administrative region of France

explanation.surface: Scotland has its own Foreign Office.
explanation.definitionFit: Ain is Scots for one's own, and also a French département named after a river near Lyon.

clue.text: Done with requirement for Poohsticks

definitions.meaning: first meaning: past and finished, best forgotten
second meaning: the game needs a stream flowing beneath a bridge

explanation.surface: Someone has finished with the needs of a children's game.
explanation.walkthrough: Poohsticks, from Winnie-the-Pooh, is played by dropping sticks off one side of a bridge and seeing whose emerges first.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means past events that are no longer worth worrying about, and literally the stream the sticks float down.

clue.text: We worked with rectors in one cathedral …

indicators.note: letters that are worked have been shaped and rearranged

explanation.surface: We collaborated with clergy inside a cathedral.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis links to the next clue, which defines another cathedral.
explanation.definitionFit: Worcester is an English city whose cathedral stands above the River Severn.

clue.text: in another, saw end of prayer cut short with entry of queen

indicators.note: the royal letter enters, going inside the observed word
cut short means the last letter is lopped off

explanation.surface: In a second cathedral, a queen arrives just as the prayers are ended.
explanation.walkthrough: Following on from 40, 'another' means another cathedral; 'saw' is the past tense of see, not a proverb or a tool.
explanation.definitionFit: Notre-Dame in Paris is a famous Gothic cathedral, so another example after the previous one.

clue.text: Batting with more confidence, one offers chance to cover

explanation.surface: A batsman, growing in confidence, gives a fielder a catching chance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cover' is a fielding position here in the surface, but means insurance cover.
explanation.definitionFit: An insurer sells policies protecting customers against risk, providing protection if bad luck strikes.

clue.text: Female, commonly odious and critical

indicators.note: commonly means as spoken in casual speech, which drops an initial aitch

explanation.surface: A vulgar woman is both nasty and fault-finding.
explanation.walkthrough: 'critical' looks like 'disapproving', but it means decisive.
explanation.definitionFit: A fateful moment is one of crucial importance with far-reaching consequences.

clue.text: In charge, one party of Africans ringed girl

indicators.note: in puts the following items inside the charge word

explanation.surface: A member of an African political party, now in charge, is engaged.
explanation.definitionFit: A fiancée wears an engagement ring, so she is a woman given a ring by her intended.

clue.text: Hardy tucks into extremely luscious sweets

indicators.note: something that tucks into another goes inside it
the extremes of a word are its two end letters

parts.note: Oliver Hardy of Laurel and Hardy

explanation.surface: A sturdy eater digs into delicious sweets.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hardy' looks like an adjective, but it is the comedian Oliver Hardy, known as Ollie.
explanation.definitionFit: Lollies are lollipops or ice lollies, and in Australia any sweets.

clue.text: Ridiculous in a suit in the country

indicators.note: something ridiculous is absurd and out of order, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: Someone looks silly wearing a suit out in the countryside.
explanation.definitionFit: Tunisia is a North African state on the Mediterranean coast.

clue.text: Excluded workers rising in turn to get drinks

indicators.note: in puts the workers inside the next item

parts.note: in British and Australian slang, your shout is your turn to buy the round

indicators.note: in a down clue, rising means the letters read upwards

explanation.surface: Workers protest at being left out when it is their round.
explanation.definitionFit: Shut out means barred or kept from entering.

clue.text: A proportion of customers sat here, troubled by notice

indicators.note: troubled means disturbed, so the letters are stirred up

explanation.surface: Some of the customers seated here are bothered by a sign.
explanation.definitionFit: Market share is the percentage of total sales in a sector that one company wins.

clue.text: Man I have heard on the radio

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a man's name

definitions.text: I have heard on the radio
definitions.meaning: second meaning: the radio operator's word for 'message received'

explanation.surface: A man says he has heard something on the wireless.
explanation.definitionFit: Roger is a male name and the voice procedure word meaning a transmission has been received.

clue.text: Short provision of beer by bar in America

parts.note: a half is half a pint of beer
Americans call a bar of music a measure

explanation.surface: A small amount of beer is served at an American bar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bar' suggests a pub, but it is a musical bar.
explanation.definitionFit: A half measure is an inadequate step that does not go far enough.

clue.text: Horrible feeling commonly looms over time

indicators.note: commonly means as said in casual speech, with the initial aitch dropped

parts.note: something that looms hangs over you

explanation.surface: A dreadful sense of foreboding often hangs over the passing hours.
explanation.definitionFit: Angst is a deep feeling of anxiety or dread.

clue.text: Trim short leggings

indicators.note: short means the word loses its last letter

explanation.surface: Cutting down a pair of leggings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Trim' looks like an instruction to cut, but it is the adjective meaning neat.
explanation.definitionFit: Tight and trim both describe something neat, compact and well kept.

clue.text: Praise silent type, advancing initially into battle

indicators.note: the earlier pieces go into the battle word

parts.note: someone who clams up says nothing

indicators.note: initially means only the first letter is used

explanation.surface: A quiet soldier is praised for moving forward first into combat.
explanation.definitionFit: Acclamation is loud, enthusiastic approval from a crowd.

clue.text: Make altogether disgusting

definitions.meaning: first meaning: earn before deductions
second meaning: total, overall
third meaning: revolting

explanation.surface: Something is made completely revolting.
explanation.walkthrough: Three separate meanings of one short word.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is a verb for earning a sum before tax, an adjective for total, and slang for revolting.

clue.text: Part of fighter's gear to lug, before run across high ground

parts.note: to cart something is to haul it
to belt is to run fast

explanation.surface: A soldier has to haul kit and run over hills.
explanation.definitionFit: A cartridge belt holds a soldier's ammunition, worn across the body or waist.

clue.text: Fielder, inadequate, returning trophies

indicators.note: returning means going back, so the letters read in reverse

parts.note: pots are cups won as prizes

explanation.surface: A poor player gives back trophies.
explanation.definitionFit: In baseball, the shortstop fields between second and third base.
